title: The logarithmic-degree conjecture for cycles with linearly many chords
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $C$ be a positive constant. A **cycle with linearly many chords** is a cycle on $[200~\ell$ vertices having at least $[201~\ell/2$ chords.

**Cycle-with-chords conjecture.** If $G$ has average degree at least $C\log\log(n)$, then $G$ contains a cycle $C$ on $[202~\ell$ vertices with at least $[203~\ell/2$ chords, for some $[204~\ell\geqslant 4$.

The surrounding discussion presents this as a conjectural strengthening of the paper's results on cycles with almost linearly many chords; it also suggests that the regular-graph case may be a natural first step. The source gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Nemanja Draganić and António Girão, “Cycles with almost linearly many chords”, arXiv:2601.08769 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08769

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).
